basis: Hydrocephalus, spasticity and intellectual disability define the neurologic disease; characteristic thumb contractures are reported in 20/20.
Myeloid blood-cell and marrow neoplasm; splenic involvement remains within the haematologic axis.
Inherited peptide or amine metabolic disorders; no additional damaged organ is common across this umbrella.
Lens abnormalities, glaucoma and skeletal/joint abnormalities define the syndrome; cardiac findings in isolated assessed cases do not establish prevalence >=30%.
Proximal tubule disease; renal hypophosphatemia and recurrent fractures each annotated 80-99%, supporting mineral and bone involvement despite less frequent rickets.
Reovirus-family infection umbrella; gastrointestinal and other organ damage vary by viral subtype.
Arrhythmogenic myocardial disease classified as an inborn mitochondrial metabolic disorder; extracardiac damage is uncommon.
Autoinflammatory arthritis; characteristic rash is transient, and cardiac, pulmonary, renal and ocular complications are each annotated below 30%.
Intracranial arachnoid cyst is a central nervous system malformation.
Malignant solitary fibrous tumor/hemangiopericytoma arising within the central nervous system.
Genetically associated immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease; no additional common organ damage is established.
Classical complement immunodeficiency; damaging discoid lupus rash in 2/2 assessed patients. Meningitis is a separately diagnosed infection.
B-cell lymphoid malignancy; lymphoma warrants both haematologic and infectious_immune axes. Mediastinal location does not establish lung damage.
Malignant neoplasm occupying the small intestine; lymphoma is only one subtype of this umbrella.
Inherited amino acid transport disorders; kidney, intestinal, ocular and neurologic damage vary across subtypes and are not universal group features.
Biotin deficiency commonly causes neurologic dysfunction and persistent dermatitis/alopecia, roughly >=30% in symptomatic disease; frequency varies by cause.
Developmental disorder with defining joint and eye abnormalities; sleep apnea 3/3 plus reported tracheomalacia support airway dysfunction. Hearing findings omitted at cap.
Neoplasm within the spinal dura involving the meningeal/nerve-root compartment, with potential spinal cord compression.
Coffin-Siris neurodevelopmental and skeletal phenotype, including growth and digital abnormalities; isolated cirrhosis and ocular reports do not establish >=30% prevalence.
Familial cortical myoclonus and epilepsy; myoclonus reflects nervous system dysfunction rather than primary skeletal muscle damage.
Autosomal recessive nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.
Pancreatic fatty replacement and duodenal stenosis/atresia affect the exocrine pancreas and intestine; no endocrine dysfunction is established.
Infectious abscess directly involving the cornea.
Intellectual disability with CNS abnormalities; ventricular septal defect and eczematoid dermatitis each reported in 1/2 patients. Estimates rest on a very small series.
MSRB3-related autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss.
